title: The Ledger Window a Circle Dues Settlement Is Counted Over
content:
## Which entries a dues settlement counts on a Circle membership

The entries counted when the dues standing on a Northbeam Circle Membership are settled are the dues
charges and the dues payments on the membership ledger, and the window they are counted over follows the
standing of the membership and what the ledger already carries.

1. Where the membership stands in grace and the ledger carries an annual dues charge booked in the twelve
   months ending on the handling day, the entries counted are the dues charges and dues payments booked in
   the month ending on the handling day.
2. Where the membership stands as an application received and the ledger carries no dues payment at all,
   the entries counted are those booked in the twenty-four months ending on the handling day.
3. Where neither of those holds, the entries counted are those booked in the twelve months ending on the
   handling day.

## The three windows as figures

| Standing and ledger | Window counted over |
|---|---|
| In grace, with an annual dues charge in the 12 months ending on the handling day | 1 month ending on the handling day |
| An application received, with no dues payment at all on the ledger | 24 months ending on the handling day |
| Neither of those | 12 months ending on the handling day |

The dues side and the payments side are both totalled over the window the membership falls in, so the two
sides are always drawn from the same window.

## Cases on the three readings

A membership standing in grace whose ledger carries an annual dues charge booked four months ago counts
only the entries of the month ending on the handling day: a payment booked five months ago falls outside
the window and does not reduce the dues side.

A membership standing in grace whose ledger carries no annual dues charge in the twelve months ending on
the handling day falls to the third reading, and the twelve months are counted.

A membership standing as an application received whose ledger carries one dues payment does not reach the
second reading, because that reading turns on the ledger carrying no dues payment at all; the twelve months
are counted instead.
